body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not always provide a minimum 12-month eligibility period for each child and does not limit termination of eligibility based on voluntary reporting to allowable reasons, as required by 98.21(a)(1). (Plan Questions 2.5.2a and 2.5.2c) • The Lead Agency does not allow for all permissible temporary changes to parents’ work, education, or training status, as required by 98.21(a)(1)(ii)(A), 98.21(a)(1)(ii)(B), 98.21(a)(1)(ii)(C), and 98.21(a)(1)(ii)(D). (Plan Question 2.5.2b) • The Lead Agency does not provide sufficient justification for the second eligibility threshold for graduated phase-out, as required by 98.21(b)(1)(ii)(A) and 98.21(b)(1)(ii)(B)(1). (Plan Questions 2.5.5cii and 2.5.5.ciii) Overall Target Completion Date: 07/01/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead agency respectfully advises that effective July 1, 2023, the following change occurred which now renders the state compliant with this regulation: Based on children being authorized during any period in a month, families may avail childcare later during the month, but the renewal period is set to 12 months which starts from initial month. This can result in less than 12 months of child care for families. The Lead Agency initiated an eligibility system Change Request that now aligns with policy to address this situation. The finalized approach now provides families with 13 months for child care when the filing date is not on the first of the month. For Intake Child Care Cases, if the Child Care Program Filing Date is not on the first of the month, then Child Care review dates are set to 13 months instead of 12 months. Policy Reference: 11004.9.5 Establishing 12- Month Authorization for Child Care 11000 Child Care Subsidy Program (delaware.gov) 01/08/2025 The lead agency respectfully advises that per policy #11004.11 Determining and Reviewing Childcare, when a family experiences a temporary change in ongoing status as working or attending job training or education program, services are continued at the same level for no less than 90 days to allow time for job search or re- engagement in a training program. Documentation regarding compliance with these provisions will be submitted. 2 The lead agency will request TA/guidance regarding compliance with provision of sufficient justification for the second eligibility threshold for graduated phase out. 02/15/2025 3 Delaware will implement action steps from the requested Technical Assistance. 07/01/2025 4 Delaware will amend its plan to document compliance. 07/01/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not provide grants or contracts for direct services for infants and toddlers, for children in underserved geographic areas, and for children with disabilities, as required by 98.30(b)(1). (Plan Questions 4.1.1c and 4.5.1i). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through November 30, 2025. • The Lead Agency has until February 6, 2025, to submit general action steps and estimated timeline related to providing grants or contracts for direct services for infants and toddlers and for children with disabilities using Appendix I of the 2025-2027 CCDF Plan. Overall Target Completion Date: 11/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency has requested a waiver regarding this provision of the New Rule. 12/30/2024 2 Delaware will fund contracts for child care programs in underserved geographic areas called Delaware’s ￿promise communities￿ in the state fiscal year 2026. Contracts will be funded for ￿seats￿ that do not supplant Purchase of Care subsidy for enrolled CCDF-eligible infants and toddlers and children with disabilities. Delaware will negotiate contracts with programs in underserved geographic areas for infant and toddler seats and children with disabilities (infant to age five) seats for State Fiscal Year 2026. 06/30/2025 3 Delaware will change its State-funded Early Care and Education policies and procedure manual for State Fiscal Year 2026. This version of the manual will be used to implement the program using braided funding. 06/30/2025 4 Delaware will verify enrollment of CCDF-eligible children in underserved geographic areas through monitoring within the month of October 2025, 30 calendar days after the start of each contracted program’s academic year. 10/31/2025 5 Delaware will pay invoices for direct services that do not supplant Purchase of Care starting in the State Fiscal Year 2026 month that aligns with Federal Fiscal Year 2026. Therefore, the first payment to meet this requirement will occur for the October 2025 month by November 30, 2025. 11/30/2025 6 Delaware will amend its plan to document compliance. 11/30/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on building and physical premises safety, including identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water and vehicular traffic for licensed centers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1e) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers for compliance with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to building and physical premises safety, including identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water and vehicular traffic, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). (Plan Question 5.5.1aii) Overall Target Completion Date: 07/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Delaware will submit evidence to the Regional Office demonstrating that the pre-service training, "Health and Safety for Child Care Professionals" training, is the same for all provider types, including family child care, large family child care, center and school-age programs. Delaware will submit evidence of the full training transcript to the Regional Office. The nine lessons of pre-service training contain content on building and physical premises safety, including identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water and vehicular traffic for licensed centers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). 02/15/2025 2 Delaware will submit evidence of its regulations and monitoring process for the required annual, unannounced inspection for licensed centers and all pre-service training, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i) and 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). This includes inspection forms. 02/15/2025 3 Delaware will request Technical Assistance to understand how to meet the requirements of 98.44(b)(1)(i) and 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). 02/15/2025 4 Delaware will implement the actions steps resulting from the requested Technical Assistance. 07/01/2026 5 Delaware will edit licensed facility regulations to comply as necessary. It will submit regulations through the following process: 1. Revise regulations. 07/01/2026 2. Submit regulation revision request to the Registrar of Regulations who moves the request through the APA process. 3. Communicate final regulations to providers, with timeline of full implementation. 4. Update all inspection forms accordingly. 6 Delaware will amend its plan to document compliance. 07/01/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency or other state agency is not the entity conducting or making eligibility determinations for all required background checks and does not ensure the privacy of the background check results, as required by 98.43(a)(1)(i) and 98.43(c)(2). (Plan Question 5.7.10) • The Lead Agency does not post all of the required information related to the interstate child abuse and neglect (CAN) registry check on their consumer education website, as required by 98.43(g) and 98.33(a)(1)(iii). (Plan Questions 5.7.15diii, 5.7.15div, 5.7.15dv, 5.7.15dvii, and 5.7.15dviii) Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 • The Lead Agency or other state agency is not the entity conducting or making eligibility determinations for all required background checks and does not ensure the privacy of the background check results, as required by 98.43(a)(1)(i) and 98.43(c)(2). (Plan Question 5.7.10) 03/21/2025 2 Delaware will submit documentation to the Regional Office to demonstrate that we are in compliance. Documentation will include example communications of provider and applicant eligibility letters and a process flow chart. Delaware will provide a demonstration of background check process to the Regional Office, including issuance of provisional eligibility notification during the on-site visit. 03/21/2025 3 • The Lead Agency does not post all of the required information related to the interstate child abuse and neglect (CAN) registry check on their 08/01/2025 consumer education website, as required by 98.43(g) and 98.33(a)(1)(iii). (Plan Questions 5.7.15diii, 5.7.15div, 5.7.15dv, 5.7.15dvii, and 5.7.15dviii) 4 Delaware will request technical assistance to understand what needs to be updated on the consumer education website. 03/21/2025 5 Delaware will implement changes to the consumer education website as a result of the requested Technical Assistance. 08/01/2025 6 Delaware will update its plan to demonstrate compliance. 08/01/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not require a qualifying result from an FBI criminal background check or an in-state criminal background check with fingerprints before a prospective staff member begins work, as required by 98.43(d)(4). (Plan Questions 5.7.12a and 5.7.12b) Overall Target Completion Date: 03/21/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Delaware will submit documentation to the Regional Office to show that we are in compliance for all licensed facility types. Documentation will include: a process flow chart, sample provisional eligibility notification, Delacare Regulations for Early Care and Education and School-Age Centers, Delacare Regulations for Family and Large Family Child Care Homes, and comprehensive background check letters for licensed centers, family child care homes, and youth camps. 03/21/2025 2 Delaware will provide a demonstration of background check process to the Regional Office, including issuance of provisional eligibility notification during the on-site visit. 03/21/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency did not sufficiently describe fiscal controls that allow for tracking of funds to establish allowable expenditures, as required by 98.67(c)(2). (Plan Question 10.1.2b) • The Lead Agency did not sufficiently describe fiscal controls to prepare and submit required reports, as required by 98.67(c)(1). (Plan Question 10.1.2c) • The Lead Agency does not sufficiently describe effective internal controls to ensure sound fiscal management, as required by 98.68(a)(1). (Plan Questions 10.1.3a and 10.1.3c) • The Lead Agency is on a corrective action plan (CAP) for an error rate over 10% reflecting that not all of its fiscal management and internal control practices are sufficiently effective, as required by 98.68(a). (Plan Questions 10.1.2, 10.1.3, 10.1.4, 10.1.5a, and 10.1.6a) Overall Target Completion Date: 04/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency will identify required state team members from each unit within the agency responsible for ensuring program integrity including members of Operations, Fiscal and the Child Care Subsidy teams. 02/28/2025 2 The lead agency will request TA on the use of the Internal Controls Self-Assessment Instrument which will assist the state in reviewing how well current policies and procedures address CCDF program integrity and financial accountability including requirements aimed at reducing payment errors, minimizing program waste, fraud, and abuse; and ensuring that funds are used for 02/28/2025 allowable program purposes and for eligible recipients. 3 The lead agency will utilize the Self-Assessment Instrument to measure the effectiveness of internal controls. 03/31/2025 4 The lead agency will follow up with recommendations to address deficiencies identified as a result of the Self-Assessment. 04/30/2025 5 The lead agency will continue to follow action steps as referenced in the Corrective Action Plan 01/15/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not sufficiently describe their organizational structure intended to ensure internal controls, as required by 98.68(a). (Plan Question 10.1.1) • The Lead Agency does not describe how effective internal controls in place include processes to identify areas of risk, as required by 98.68(a)(2). (Plan Question 10.1.4a) • The Lead Agency does not describe how the Lead Agency evaluates the effectiveness of its internal controls, as required by 98.68(a)(4). (Plan Questions 10.1.6a and 10.1.6b) Overall Target Completion Date: 04/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency will identify required state team members from each unit within the agency responsible for ensuring program integrity including members of the Operations, Fiscal and the Child Care Subsidy teams. 02/28/2025 2 The lead agency will request TA on the use of the Internal Controls Self-Assessment Instrument which will assist the state in reviewing how well current policies and procedures address CCDF program integrity and financial accountability including requirements aimed at reducing payment errors, minimizing program waste, fraud, and abuse; and 02/28/2025 ensuring that funds are used for allowable program purposes and for eligible recipients. 3 The lead agency will utilize the Self-Assessment Instrument to measure the effectiveness of internal controls. 03/31/2025 4 The lead agency will follow up with recommendations to address deficiencies identified as a result of the Self-Assessment. 04/30/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not include the results of activities to identify program violations, as required by 98.68(b)(1). (Plan Question 10.2.1) • The Lead Agency does not include the results of activities to investigate and recover fraudulent payments, as required by 98.68(b)(2). (Plan Question 10.2.2b) • The Lead Agency does not include the results of activities to impose sanctions on clients or providers in response to fraud, as required by 98.68(b)(2). (Plan Question 10.2.2e) Overall Target Completion Date: 01/08/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead agency respectfully advises that per our current policy/procedure, substantiated cases of fraud or intentional program violation by a parent/caretaker will result termination from the childcare subsidy program. Policy Citation: 1104.12 Closing Child Care Cases; 11005.2 Parent/Caretaker Responsibilities; 11005.4 Child Care Overpayments; 11006.4.3 Clients Who Fail to Pay Child Care Fee, 11006.5 Termination. When provider fraud or intentional program 01/08/2025 violation is substantiated, the lead agency has the right to withhold payment and/or terminate the childcare subsidy contract. Policy Citation: 11006.1 Service Providers; 11006.5.1 Terminating Providers and Self- Arranged Clients 11000 Child Care Subsidy Program (delaware.gov) 2 The lead agency will amend the plan to include verbiage regarding inclusion of the results of activities to identify program violations. 01/31/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not provide aggregate data on the number of serious injuries, number of deaths, number of substantiated child abuse instances that occurred in licensed youth camps considered child care settings, or the total number of children in care for all licensed youth camps, as required by 98.33(a)(5)(ii). (Plan Questions 9.2.5ai, 9.2.5aii, 9.2.5aiii, and 9.2.5aiv) Overall Target Completion Date: 02/15/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Delaware runs its calendar-year report on the aggregate data for the number of serious injuries, number of deaths, and number of substantiated child abuse instances that occurred in licensed facilities by January 15th of the subsequent calendar year. Delaware will run the report on the aggregate data on the number of serious injuries, number of deaths, number of substantiated child abuse instances that occurred in licensed youth camps considered child care settings, or the total number 01/15/2025 of children in care for all licensed youth camps by January 15, 2025. 2 Delaware will update its website to show the reported totals for licensed youth camps. It will add a space for the yearly aggregate data on the number of serious injuries, number of deaths, number of substantiated child abuse instances that occurred in licensed youth camps considered child care settings, or the total number of children in care for all licensed youth camps, as required by 98.33(a)(5)(ii). 02/15/2025
